issues.issue: "Securities" is defined to include "securities or other assets", a catch-all whose reach against the enumerated word "securities" is uncertain. The scope of what may be transferred under a Transaction therefore has no fixed boundary.

The insolvency list ends in the general catch-all "or similar law" and "similar official", so whether a given foreign or regulatory proceeding falls inside the enumerated bankruptcy/receivership specifics is open to ejusdem generis argument.

The definition's only content is a cross-reference to "Paragraph 4(_)" which is illegible/garbled, so the subparagraph that generates Additional Purchased Securities is not identified on the face of the definition.

In the absence of agreement the deadline is "established in accordance with market practice", a standard with no named source or benchmark. Whether a margin call was timely therefore turns on an undefined market custom.

"Market Value" turns on a "price ... obtained from a generally recognized source agreed to by the parties or the most recent closing bid quotation from such a source", leaving open both what qualifies as a generally recognized source and what happens when no source has been agreed; the trailing "unless contrary to market practice" adds a further undefined override. For illiquid mortgage securities two parties can plausibly reach very different values on this wording.

The definition requires a source "agreed to by the parties", whereas the flush language of Paragraph 11(d) lets the nondefaulting party "establish the source therefor in its sole discretion"; the two cannot easily be squared when valuing the same securities on default.

Annex VI §10 directs that references to "Repurchase Price" be read as "Repurchase Price or the Sell Back Price", which sits awkwardly with this definition's fixed Purchase Price plus Price Differential formula.
Transactions may be agreed "orally", which leaves the existence and terms of a binding Transaction provable outside any writing. The provision gives no test for when the oral agreement is complete.
The Confirmation is "conclusive evidence" unless "specific objection is made promptly after receipt", and "promptly" is given no measure. Whether an objection was timely is left entirely at large.
Demand must be made "no later than such time as is customary in accordance with market practice", an undefined external standard governing when a Transaction validly terminates.

The margin call turns on "aggregate Market Value" and on "additional Securities reasonably acceptable to Buyer", both of which leave the size and satisfaction of the call to contested judgment. Neither the valuation nor the acceptability standard is fixed by the paragraph.

The trigger depends wholly on the Paragraph 2(j) "Market Value" definition, which requires a pricing source "agreed to by the parties"; where no source was agreed, Paragraph 4(a) supplies no fallback and cannot be applied on its own terms.

Performance is fixed by "the close of business in the relevant market" and by the Margin Notice Deadline, which itself defaults to market practice; whether a transfer was late thus depends on undefined market conventions.

Annex I §3 removes Buyer's Paragraph 5(ii) election entirely and Annex VI §9 disapplies Paragraph 5 to Buy/Sell Back Transactions, so this paragraph's stated Buyer discretion is displaced by two later provisions.

Paragraph 8 states that "[a]ll of Seller's interest in the Purchased Securities shall pass to Buyer on the Purchase Date", which pulls against this paragraph's deemed pledge and security interest if the Transactions are recharacterised as loans.
Segregation is required only "[t]o the extent required by applicable law", an open-ended qualifier that makes the obligation's existence depend on an unspecified legal test.

The disclosure is left in unexecuted template form with unselected bracketed alternatives ([will]/[may], [its clearing bank]/[third parties], [the clearing]/[any] lien), so its operative content cannot be read off the page.

Annex I §4(c) grants Seller a unilateral right to substitute subject only to Buyer's election to refuse, which does not sit comfortably with 9(a)'s requirement of Buyer's prior "agreement with and acceptance".

Paragraph 9(a) makes substitution conditional on Buyer's agreement and acceptance while 9(b) deems that acceptance already given in seller-custody Transactions; the two subparagraphs point in opposite directions on the same act.

The Events of Default are an exhaustive enumeration with no cure period for items (i)-(iii), inviting expressio unius argument about failures not listed. Whether a mere failure to meet a margin call is instantly a default is left to the bare list.
Notice of the exercise of the option need only be given "as promptly as practicable" and is excused entirely on an Act of Insolvency, leaving the timing requirement without a measurable content.

The liquidation remedy is governed by "in a recognized market (or otherwise in a commercially reasonable manner) at such price or prices as the nondefaulting party may reasonably deem satisfactory", and alternatively by a price "obtained from a generally recognized source" chosen in the party's "sole discretion"; each of those standards is contestable and they pull in different directions. A defaulting seller and a liquidating buyer can read the same words to permit and to forbid the same sale or mark.

The credit alternative in (B) uses a price from "a generally recognized source" chosen unilaterally, whereas Paragraph 2(j) defines Market Value by reference to a source "agreed to by the parties"; the two valuation regimes for the same securities are hard to reconcile.

The parties deem all Securities to be "instruments traded in a recognized market" and let the nondefaulting party pick a pricing source "in its sole discretion", which is an unbounded grant sitting on a factual premise that may be untrue for illiquid securities.

The deemed acknowledgment that a recognized market always exists undercuts the alternative "or otherwise in a commercially reasonable manner" limb of Paragraph 11(d)(i), which assumes there may be no such market.

The cap on Repurchase Price increases is expressly limited to Transactions "in respect of which the defaulting party is acting as Buyer", inviting an expressio unius argument that no equivalent cap applies to a defaulting Seller.

After the two enumerated damages heads the clause adds "any other loss, damage, cost or expense directly arising or resulting from" the default, a catch-all whose reach against the specifics (and the meaning of "directly") is uncertain.

The blanket cross-Transaction setoff and netting right is expressly negated for Funds by Annex VII §1(a) and (c) and limited as against an Agent by Annex IV §3(b), so the "single agreement" premise is not uniform across the instrument.

Notices "may" be given by any of several methods and "may be made orally, to be confirmed promptly in writing", so the clause prescribes no mandatory or effective-on-receipt method for critical notices such as margin calls.

The clause supersedes only prior agreements "containing general terms and conditions for repurchase transactions", so it is not a full integration clause and its scope against other prior dealings is uncertain.
Paragraph 15(b) permits a party to assign or charge its interest in sums payable under Paragraph 11 notwithstanding this prohibition, leaving the boundary of the ban to be worked out.

The requirement that any modification or consent be in a writing executed by both parties sits uneasily with Paragraph 3(a), which allows Transactions to be agreed orally, and with Paragraph 13, which allows notices and requests to be made orally.
"[N]o material adverse change in Seller's financial condition" is a deemed representation with no threshold or measure of materiality.

The recognition is qualified by "except insofar as the type of Securities ... or the term ... would render such definition inapplicable", a self-cancelling proviso whose operation is left to be worked out case by case.

This section declares Annexes III-VII and Schedules III.A and VII.A to "form a part of this Agreement and ... be applicable", yet Schedule III.A is a blank "[Insert provisions applicable to relevant country]" template and Schedule VII.A lists no Funds or Custodians, so annexes that presuppose completed schedules are switched on with nothing in them.

This clause says Annex I governs over any inconsistency with "the Agreement", but Annex VI §1 and the conflict sentence in Annex VII each provide that those Annexes prevail over "any other term of the Agreement"; the priority rules are circular.

This section abolishes the Paragraph 5(ii) election that Paragraph 5 of the Agreement expressly confers on Buyer, and Annex VI §9 in turn disapplies Paragraph 5 altogether to Buy/Sell Back Transactions.

"[S]ubstantially the same Securities" is the operative test for permitted substitution and is nowhere defined, and the notice deadline refers to "such business day" with no antecedent day identified. Both leave the mechanics of a substitution notice open to opposing readings.

The subparagraph is triggered where "Seller exercises its right to substitute or terminate under subparagraph (c)", but (c) gives Seller no termination right — it says only that Buyer "shall offer Seller the right to terminate"; the cross-reference does not match the clause it invokes.

The definition is stated to apply "[f]or purposes of the Agreement" but every limb is conditioned on an International Transaction, so "business day" — used throughout Paragraphs 4 and 11 — is left undefined for ordinary domestic Transactions.
Paragraphs 4(c) and 11(iv) of the Agreement impose deadlines by reference to "business day" although this Annex III definition, the only one in the instrument, covers only International Transactions.
"LIBOR plus a spread, as may be specified" leaves the spread open, so if none is specified in a Confirmation the substituted Prime Rate has no determinable value.

The proviso limits the term "Tax" "for purposes of Paragraphs 5 and 6" without saying whether those are Paragraphs 5 and 6 of the Agreement (Income Payments and Security Interest) or of Annex III (Taxes and Tax Event). The cross-reference is genuinely two-way.
"[A]ny circumstance known or reasonably known to it" is an unusual and imprecise formulation of the knowledge standard triggering the notice duty.
The trigger is that the Change of Tax Law will, "in the notifying party's reasonable opinion, have a material adverse effect", combining a subjective opinion with an undefined materiality threshold.

The bar on "any sum constituting consequential loss or damage" uses a term of notoriously contested meaning, and it is not reconciled with the indemnity for "reasonable legal and other professional expenses" in the same sentence.

Paragraph 10(ii) of the Agreement has each party represent that it will act as principal unless agency is agreed in writing in advance, whereas this Annex is declared applicable by Annex I §1 to "all transactions" in which a party acts as agent.

The counterparty may reject a Principal it determines "in its sole discretion" to be unacceptable, an unbounded power to unwind a concluded Transaction. The clause gives no standard against which that determination can be tested.
The removal of any right of setoff against the Agent pulls against the unrestricted setoff and netting rights conferred by Paragraph 12 (Single Agreement).
Paragraph 4(a)-(b) of the Agreement calculates margin on an aggregate basis across all Transactions, whereas this subparagraph requires a Transaction-by-Transaction determination.
Treating each Principal as party to a separate Agreement for default remedies cuts against the cross-Transaction default and netting premise of Paragraph 12 (Single Agreement).

Deeming both Agent and Principals "parties" and treating an Act of Insolvency of the Agent as an Event of Default of the Principal is difficult to reconcile with Annex IV §3(a), which says the Agent does not guarantee its Principal's performance.

"Forward Exposure" is a hypothetical replacement-cost loss "determined in accordance with market practice" where the parties have not agreed otherwise, with no method, source or determining party specified.

Collateral must be "reasonably acceptable to the In-the-Money-Party" and sufficient by Market Value to eliminate an exposure that is itself only measurable by market practice, so the size and adequacy of a call are both left at large.

An Event of Default arises on failure to perform "any covenant or obligation" under "Paragraph 2 or any other provision of this Annex", a catch-all with no materiality filter sitting behind a single specific cross-reference.

Liquidation of Forward Collateral is governed by "in a recognized market (or otherwise in a commercially reasonable manner) at such price or prices as the nondefaulting party may reasonably deem satisfactory", the same open-textured standard used for Purchased Securities, and by a price from an unnamed "generally recognized source". Whether a given sale or mark meets it is contestable on the words alone.

The purchase of Replacement Securities is at prices the nondefaulting party "may reasonably deem satisfactory", or at a deemed price obtained from "a generally recognized source" in its "sole discretion", so the defaulting party's liability is fixed by a standard with no external anchor.

The parties deem all Forward Collateral to be "instruments traded in a recognized market" and allow the nondefaulting party to fix a pricing source "in its sole discretion", which is both a counterfactual premise and an unbounded discretion.

The provision preserves the right to give notice under "subparagraph (a), (b), (c) or (d) of Paragraph 2", but only subparagraph (a) of Annex V Paragraph 2 actually provides for the giving of a notice.
This clause makes Annex VI prevail over "any other term of the Agreement", while Annex I §2 makes Annex I govern over any inconsistency with the Agreement; each purports to trump the other.

The whole operation of the paragraph turns on whether including Accrued Interest is "contrary to market practice with respect to the Securities", an undefined external test that switches between two different pricing formulas.

This section disapplies Paragraph 5 of the Agreement to Buy/Sell Back Transactions and reverses the flow of Income, which cannot be reconciled with Annex I §3, a provision that mandates Buyer transfer Income to Seller under Paragraph 5(i).
The clause reads "In 11 of the Agreement", omitting the word "Paragraph", so the reference must be supplied by inference.

"Fund" is defined by reference to the investment companies "identified on Schedule VII.A", but Schedule VII.A in this executed instrument names no Fund and no Custodian, so the Annex declared applicable by Annex I §1 has no subject.
This sentence gives Annex VII priority over "any other term of the Agreement" while Annex I §2 gives Annex I priority over any inconsistent term of the Agreement, leaving no way to rank the two.

Applying margin and the single-agreement provisions "based solely upon Transactions entered into by a particular Fund" directly negates Paragraph 12's premise that all Transactions form one contractual relationship with cross-Transaction netting.

The flat denial of setoff between Funds contradicts Paragraph 12(ii) of the Agreement, which entitles each party to set off claims in respect of any Transaction against obligations under any other Transaction.

The Buyer's Margin Percentage is left as a blank "at least _%" while the proviso says it may in no event be less than 100%, so the operative figure is missing and the two limbs of the sentence do not fit together. The second sentence then fixes the "Buyer's" Margin Percentage for Transactions in which the Fund is Seller, apparently in place of the Seller's Margin Percentage.
Delivery must be to the Custodian "designated for such Fund in Schedule VII.A", yet Schedule VII.A designates no Custodian, so the mechanic cannot be performed as written.

The Schedule states that the Agreement "is entered into by or on behalf of the following Funds" but the table of Funds and Custodians is blank, which cannot be squared with Annex VII's definition of "Fund" or with Annex I §1 declaring Annex VII and this Schedule applicable.
